narrative.overview: Images lie on a bright, cool, backlit surface and decisions are made by marking them. The ground is cool paper-white, every image sits in a black frame like a contact-sheet negative, and the owner's judgement shows up as grease-pencil marks drawn over the frame rather than as verb buttons.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground, pure-white sheets, ink-black borders; square corners.
Every image lives in a near-black frame with a mono edge-code strip.
Decision colour is semantic and rare: vermilion pick, amber maybe, slate reject.
Active state is always inversion to solid ink with white text.
One paper-lift shadow; otherwise depth comes from borders.

rules.name: The Marks-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour means a decision (pick, maybe, reject) or a status. Never use vermilion, amber or slate as decoration or as a generic accent.

rules.name: The Ink Inversion Rule
rules.body: Hover, selected, pressed and current states invert to ink fill with white text; they do not tint.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Any count, time, score or frame number is JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Heavy-Tight Rule
rules.body: Headings are 800 weight with negative letter-spacing; never light weights.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: The only shadow is the soft paper lift, used for things that float above the sheet. No hard offset shadows, no glow.

dos: Do put every image in a frame-black frame with an edge-code strip.
Do express keep, maybe and reject with the grease-pencil mark family in vermilion, amber and slate.
Do invert hover and selected states to ink fill with white text.
Do set every number, time and count in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do keep corners square and borders 1px (controls) or 2px (structure).
Do keep a visible 3px vermilion focus outline.
donts: Don't use dark sidebar dashboards or dark page grounds; the table is light, only frames are dark.
Don't use vermilion, amber or slate for decoration or non-decision accents.
Don't add shadows beyond the paper lift, or any hard offset shadow.
Don't round buttons, inputs or cards.
Don't replace decision marks with verb-only coloured buttons.
